sit-1.question: Why can't Kani verify Ply's targets, and does routing bounded checks to Kani survive contact with real code?

hypotheses.statement: The true explanation is not in the current candidate set
Heap-allocating std collections (BTreeSet/Vec/String) are the specific blocker: CBMC symbolically unwinds their generic allocation/clone/sort algorithms, and code avoiding them verifies fine
predictedEvidence: scalar and small-struct targets verify in ~0.1s
replacing BTreeSet with a bitmask changes the failure mode
fixed-size arrays verify where Vec of the same length does not
the stall trace names collection internals like clone_subtree or median3_rec

hypotheses.statement: Our harnesses are written wrong (unbounded symbolic length, missing kani::any_vec, missing unwind bounds), so this is a fixture defect not a Kani limit
predictedEvidence: a Vec bounded to length 1 still times out, which is absurd for a genuine capability limit
using Kanis dedicated bounded-collection helpers fixes it
the same shape verifies when constructed differently

hypotheses.statement: Recursion in the target is the real cost driver, independent of collections: CBMC cannot bound recursive descent through a tree structure
predictedEvidence: a single leaf verifies but one level of recursion does not
depth 1 vs 2 vs 3 shows a sharp cliff

hypotheses.statement: Bounded model checking simply does not scale to ordinary Rust at all: any target beyond toy scalars is intractable regardless of shape, and routing bounded to Kani is unviable as designed
predictedEvidence: fixed-size arrays time out too, not just Vec
Option/Result of scalars are already slow
no configuration (unwind, solver, object-bits) helps anywhere

hypotheses.statement: It is a configuration and flag problem: the right unwind bounds, solver choice, or stubbing makes these targets tractable and we have not found the recipe
predictedEvidence: a solver swap or object-bits change flips a timeout to verified
Kani docs name a supported recipe we have not applied
-Z stubbing of collection ops makes the kernel provable

observations.text: M0 spike: scalar and small-struct contract proofs verify in 0.05-0.11s each (private fn, method with old(), struct with public fields)
Ply's own verdict kernel (pure, 300 lines, BTreeSet+Vec+Option<Vec<String>> fields) never returns a verdict; CBMC trace names BTreeMap clone_subtree unwinding

Intervention: replaced the kernel's BTreeSet status field with a u8 bitmask. Failure mode changed from indefinite hang to deterministic timeout at 5min; trace moved to String sort/median3_rec in the assumptions Vec
Intervention: tried unwind bounds 2 and 3, --object-bits 8, and the kissat solver on the kernel harnesses. None changed the outcome materially
Scale sweep first result: Vec<u8> bounded to length <= 1 with a sum contract did not verify within 120s
